correctness.rationale: Every invariant prism matching is a union of rung or paired-horizontal edge orbits and extends by adding all available rungs; the geometric fixed-point subspace is the whiskered matching complex. A cover by rung closed stars has a full simplex nerve with nonempty contractible intersections. Exactly the base perfect-matchings are facets outside this contractible core, with all proper faces inside. Thus quotient is the claimed sphere wedge, including the S^0 case. Relative integral chains form a freely generated top degree module and give the oriented permutation action; tested with exhaustive small prism enumeration and mod-two Lefschetz checks.

value.rationale: The fixed-point topology for an involution on a recently studied prism perfect-matching complex is governed exactly by the base graph’s perfect-matching count for every finite graph. The theorem supplies a natural PL identification, an exact nonequivariant homotopy type and integral homology representation, and the complete oriented integral automorphism homology lattice. It applies to nonouterplanar graphs and separates equivariant information from known nonequivariant classifications; this is structurally motivated, not a numerical toy or arbitrary slice.
